completion:
Eliminate all raw data from observations when the tests were conducted in the midst of heavy industrial activity (e.g., during working hours when emissions are at peak volumes).
3. Eliminate all raw data from observation when methanol concentrations exceeded safe drinking and residential emission standards (e.g., 2 mg/L).
4. Eliminate all raw data from observations when the sampling locations were located well within the bounds of the community (e.g., within 1 and 3 km of the industrial site).
5. To minimize exposure to litigation, ensure that your sampling locations are located away from the heavy industrial concentrations (e.g., 200 m upline from the site's smokestacks).
6. For sanity's sake, limit your sampling locations to those that fall within the realm of statistical relevance.
7. Check your work to confirm that all data collected actually coincide with the sampling plan submitted to relevant state agencies
